title: quality-drift-1on1-prep-morgan-jun09
content:
Purpose: quick prep for 1:1 with Avery — focus on recent quality drift flagged by nightly evals, triage A/B batch, and decide next actions (rollback, prompt tweak, or accept trade-off).

Top-line notes (what I found overnight):
- Nightly eval pipeline surfaced a 5.8% drop in 'helpfulness' pass rate on the customer-support prompt set (prompt-set: csv2-unified).
- Regression coincides with config change: model variant switched from gptx-qa-q4_1 to gptx-qa-q4_2 on 2026-06-07 (autoscaler rollout + quantization tweak).
- A/B run (2026-06-08): 12k samples; A (q4_1) baseline, B (q4_2) new. Metric diffs: accuracy +0.2% but helpfulness -6.1%, toxicity unchanged.
- Error logs show slightly longer tokenization latency for some long-context queries (>=1024 tokens), likely due to changed tokenizer config in the new runtime image.

Immediate checks to run during 1:1 (quick commands / where to look):
- Evaluate per-customer cohort (enterprise vs free): SQL: SELECT cohort, count(*) as n, avg(helpful_flag) FROM evals.nightly WHERE date >= '2026-06-06' AND prompt_set = 'csv2-unified' GROUP BY cohort;
- Confirm rollout percentage/time windows in rollout logs: /infra/rollouts/service-rollout-logs (filter by model tag gptx-qa-q4_2).
- Compare token distribution for failing cases: run sample-token-hist.py on B-fails-20260608.jsonl (stored in /tmp/evals/).
- Sanity run: re-run 500 random failing queries on both variants locally (docker image: redwood/runtime:gptx-q4_2-canary).

Agenda (20 min):
- 0-4m: quick recap of what triggered alert + metric summary (I present).
- 4-10m: show examples (3-5 difficult cases) that illustrate helpfulness drop (we should pick varied lengths and intents).
- 10-14m: discuss probable root cause hypotheses (quantization precision, tokenizer change, rollout smearing).
- 14-18m: decide mitigation path (rollback vs targeted prompt patch vs narrow canary).
- 18-20m: assign actions + deadlines.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Tokenizer/config mismatch: new runtime image shipped a minor tokenizer normalization change that affects answer framing for support prompts (evidence: longer token counts in fails).
2) Quantization edge-case: q4_2 kernel selection causes rare softmax truncation for some contexts (evidence: accuracy slightly up overall but semantics shifted).
3) Data skew in A/B sample: more long-context enterprise tickets happened to be in B bucket (evidence: preliminary cohort SQL shows enterprise skew).
4) Prompt canonicalization difference in deployment pipeline (older prompt normalization removed punctuation — check PR #482).

Rollback decision framework (quick checklist):
- If helpfulness drop > 5% across >10k evals and enterprise cohort impacted -> immediate rollback to q4_1 and open incident (P1).
- If drop isolated to long-context (>1024) with <2% overall impact -> narrow canary / prompt patch and monitor 48h.
- If drop correlated with specific prompt template -> patch prompt set, run targeted evals, push canary.

Proposed immediate actions (I will take these if we agree):
- Morgan: re-run the local 500-sample sanity check and attach side-by-side outputs (due: 2026-06-10 15:00).
- Avery: check rollout logs and confirm the exact timestamp/percentage ramp for gptx-qa-q4_2 (due: 2026-06-10 12:00).
- Diego: run model-level perf telemetry to extract kernel selection histogram for q4_1 vs q4_2 (due: 2026-06-10 18:00).
- If results point to tokenizer change, escalate to infra-runtime team and open a blocker PR to revert tokenizer config in image (owner: Avery, due: 2026-06-11 EOD).

Longer-term follow-ups (write down here so we don't forget):
- Add a focused eval for "helpfulness under long-context" to nightly suite (owner: me + Diego). Include stratified buckets: <=256, 257-1024, >1024.
- Improve canary sampling to ensure cohort parity across A/B runs (product + infra ticket).
- Add a preflight check in CI to compare token counts for golden prompts when changing runtime images.
- Build a quick dashboard: "eval drift watch" that surfaces >3% drops with cohort breakdown and recent related rollout IDs.

Examples to show in meeting (shortlist) - pick 3: 
- Case 1: (long kernel) user-ticket id 9c4a — B answer is terse and deflects, A gives step-by-step remediation.
- Case 2: (ambiguous intent) id 3b7f — B hallucinates config field name; A is correct.
- Case 3: (short prompt) id 21aa — both okay (shows not everything regressed).

Notes to self:
- Keep the tone collaborative in the 1:1; frame as "triage + safe decision" not blame.
- If we rollback, make sure support and CS are looped and a short public-facing note is drafted with keyline on SLA/impact.

Outstanding questions for Avery:
- Was there any other infra patch at 2026-06-07 besides model image? (e.g., loader, tokenizer lib)
- Do we have a quick way to force-run only enterprise cohort through nightly evals?

Misc scratch (todo if we have time):
- Draft a 1-paragraph incident note template for internal channel (who, what, impact, mitigation, follow-ups).
- Add a small eval harness to compare answer tokenization boundaries side-by-side (script idea: diff-tokenized-outputs.py).

OK — that's it. Keep this doc as my running scratch pad; will prune before moving to shared drive incident doc if we escalate.
summary: 1:1 prep for quality-drift triage: regression in helpfulness after model variant rollout; hypotheses, quick checks, rollback criteria, concrete immediate actions and owners.
